structured_requirement.description: A single-camera parking-entrance plate-localization appliance. A MIPI CSI-2 camera supplies frames and is configured through I2C/SCCB; Ethernet connects the appliance to a parking-management host. The application converts the image to grayscale and uses top-hat/black-hat morphology, Sobel filtering, smoothing, thresholding and feature combination to extract likely plate regions. The host receives candidate-mask or region data for downstream handling. Character segmentation, OCR, authorization decisions and barrier actuation are outside the current benchmark.

benchmark_context.workload: Current source macros define 128x128 input with four channels, despite an older main comment mentioning 256x256. The main test initializes a black frame and returns a candidate image; richer deployment images require separate validation.
benchmark_context.scenario_status: Proposed single-camera parking deployment; MIPI reception, Ethernet transport and sensor-control drivers are integration requirements, not implemented benchmark features.
benchmark_context.validation_target: Compare the candidate mask with the CPU reference for the same frames. Plate-reading accuracy is not an available correctness metric for this localization-only program.
benchmark_context.resource_note: Use the 13 mm^2 small-CPU budget for Ibex-oriented mapping, together with the existing 75 MHz and 28nm experiment settings; candidate IP suggestions do not fix the CPU or choose application hotspots.

communication.requirements: Require one MIPI CSI-2 digital camera receiver with frame markers and pixel-stream input. UART, SPI and an I2C controller alone do not satisfy camera pixel acquisition.
Require an I2C/SCCB sensor-register controller for exposure, gain and capture-mode configuration of the single parking camera.
Require Ethernet communication to send plate-candidate masks or region records and receive capture/configuration requests from a parking-management host. Do not replace Ethernet with UART or SPI.

debug.requirements: Require hardware cycle and transaction counters for measuring capture, buffer transfer and plate-localization latency.

analog.requirements: Use a digital camera module with sensor-side conversion; no analog pixel ADC is required.

audio.requirements: Parking plate localization has no audio function.

video.requirements: Require frame buffering with double buffering and row stride, so capture and plate-region processing can use separate image buffers. No display controller or reusable OCR engine is required.

bus.requirements: Require on-chip SRAM scratchpad storage for grayscale, morphology intermediates and candidate masks; determine capacity from the compiled image dimensions and buffer lifetimes.
Require an AXI shared-memory interconnect supporting burst transfers between camera buffers, CPU and application accelerators.
Require AXI-Lite start, completion and parameter registers for CPU-controlled processing.

structured_requirement.description: An industrial green-marker localization node attached to a conveyor or positioning fixture. An external smart-camera module delivers already formatted BGR frames through SPI. The node converts BGR to HSV, thresholds the configured green range, dilates the mask, and filters connected regions by geometry to report target presence and center coordinates over UART. It is a color/region detector, not a neural-network classifier or license-plate OCR engine. The production interface carries compact coordinates, without a local video display.

benchmark_context.workload: Current source defaults: 320x240 BGR input with three 8-bit channels. The built-in test constructs a green rectangle and prints detection status and center coordinates.
benchmark_context.scenario_status: Proposed SPI/UART deployment; the benchmark currently constructs its input in memory and does not implement the physical camera link.
benchmark_context.validation_target: Compare target presence and integer center coordinates against the CPU reference; compare intermediate masks when validating an accelerator.
benchmark_context.resource_note: Retain the existing experimental resource limits. Green-marker localization does not imply a measured conveyor speed or a guaranteed real-time deadline.

communication.requirements: Require an SPI slave interface for receiving fixed-length 320x240 BGR frames from an external camera processor. The external processor owns the sensor, exposure and pixel formatting. Do not substitute I2C sensor control or a MIPI raw-camera receiver for SPI frame input.
Require a UART interface for target-present flags, integer X/Y coordinates and threshold configuration. No continuous frame transmission or Ethernet network stack is required.

debug.requirements: Require JTAG debug access for CPU bring-up, firmware inspection and detector validation. A bus trace recorder is not a required production component.

analog.requirements: The external camera module digitizes the image; no on-chip ADC is needed.

audio.requirements: The node reports coordinates and has no audio function.

video.requirements: Require a frame buffer for a single 320x240 BGR image with deterministic row stride. Color conversion and mask morphology remain application processing functions; do not require a reusable ISP or display IP to perform them.

bus.requirements: Require local SRAM scratchpad access for HSV data, the binary mask and dilation temporary storage; preserve byte-addressed arrays.
Require AXI-Lite control and status registers for CPU-invoked processing, with completion visible before reading coordinates.

structured_requirement.description: A USB-connected desktop document-cleanup appliance for digitizing receipts and forms. A host scanner supplies digital RGB page images over USB; the appliance returns a cleaned binary mask and document bounding box over the same connection. The scan application performs grayscale conversion, histogram equalization, Sobel edge detection, adaptive thresholding, morphological closing, feature merging, and document-region extraction. Operation is page-triggered, with no continuous video capture or local display. OCR and text recognition are outside this application's scope.

benchmark_context.workload: Current source defaults: 256x256 RGB input, 8-bit channels; binary mask and four-coordinate bounding box outputs. The host test reads PPM/PGM or uses a built-in image.
benchmark_context.scenario_status: Proposed deployment requirements derived from the application; the benchmark does not implement USB transport.
benchmark_context.validation_target: Compare the output mask, bounding box, active-pixel count and checksum against the CPU reference using the same input.
benchmark_context.resource_note: Preserve the existing 75 MHz, 28nm and 25 mm^2 experimental settings; no new measured throughput or page-rate claim.

communication.demand: USB page input and result output
communication.requirements: Require a USB device controller for host-to-device RGB page transfer and device-to-host binary masks and bounding boxes. The host owns scanner acquisition. SPI, I2C, UART and Ethernet are not substitutes for this USB data connection.
Require memory-to-stream and stream-to-memory DMA with explicit transfer lengths for page input and mask output; notify the CPU at page-transfer completion.

debug.requirements: Require hardware cycle and transaction counters to measure page transfer and processing time; continuous instruction trace is not required.

analog.requirements: Input is already digitized by the external scanner; no scanner ADC or analog image frontend is required.

audio.requirements: Document cleanup has no audio input or output.

video.requirements: Require frame-buffer storage with line-stride handling for one RGB page and its grayscale and binary processing buffers. The current benchmark uses 256x256 pixels. No MIPI sensor receiver, display controller, video codec or OCR IP is required.

bus.requirements: Require SRAM scratchpad storage for grayscale images, binary masks and neighborhood-processing temporary buffers. Size it from the application arrays; do not infer capacity from a generic IP name.
Require AXI-Lite memory-mapped start, completion and status registers for CPU-controlled page processing.

structured_requirement.description: An airborne wide-area imagery processing payload for on-board foreground detection from consecutive camera frames. The application debayers raw pixels, forms grayscale images, registers each frame against a template with iterative Lucas-Kanade processing, warps images, and updates persistent Gaussian-mixture background models to identify foreground pixels. A MIPI CSI-2 camera and I2C sensor control feed the payload; Ethernet carries foreground masks and registration/status records to an on-board mission computer. Temporal model state and multi-pass image access distinguish this workload from a single-frame detector. Video compression and object tracking are outside the implemented pipeline.

benchmark_context.workload: Current synthetic test: three 36x36 Bayer source frames, a 32x32 processing region, five GMM models per pixel and 20 Lucas-Kanade iterations. Image and model processing use floating-point data.
benchmark_context.scenario_status: Airborne payload interfaces and external memory are proposed deployment requirements. The small synthetic benchmark does not demonstrate full-resolution wide-area throughput.
benchmark_context.validation_target: Compare foreground masks/counts, registration results and persistent model outputs with the CPU reference over the full frame sequence. Define floating-point tolerances before hardware acceptance.
benchmark_context.resource_note: DDR is a deployment capacity requirement for temporal frame/model state, not a claim that the current small test needs off-chip capacity. Retain the existing 25 mm^2 and 75 MHz targets.

communication.requirements: Require a MIPI CSI-2 receiver for raw Bayer pixel streams with frame synchronization. Preserve raw samples for application-level debayering; a host command interface alone is insufficient.
Require I2C/SCCB sensor-register access for exposure, gain and frame timing on the airborne camera.

Require Ethernet communication for foreground-mask blocks, registration records and configuration messages to an on-board mission computer. SPI or UART metadata links alone do not meet this network-interface requirement.
Require burst-capable streaming DMA to transfer current/reference frames and persistent GMM state between shared memory and processing units; preserve frame ordering.

debug.requirements: Require a timestamped trace monitor for CPU, DMA and processing events to diagnose iterative-registration stalls and frame-sequence processing. A plain serial console alone is insufficient.

analog.requirements: The payload receives digitized Bayer samples; no analog acquisition frontend is required.

audio.requirements: Airborne imagery analysis has no microphone, codec or audio output.

video.requirements: Require strided frame-buffer access to current and reference frames, with independent buffers retained across frames. Keep application debayering, registration and GMM processing in the software/accelerator flow; no video encoder or display controller is required.

bus.requirements: Require a DDR memory controller for deployment-scale current/reference images and persistent per-pixel multi-model state. Capacity must be derived from deployment resolution and model count, not from an assumed fixed IP capacity.
Require a burst-capable AXI interconnect for CPU, DMA, DDR and multiple processing masters accessing frame and model buffers.
Require local SRAM scratchpad for gradient tiles, warped-image tiles and small registration matrices, separate from persistent external frame/model storage.
Require AXI-Lite configuration and completion registers for sequencing frame-processing stages.

structured_requirement.description: A local dual-sensor night-viewing terminal for low-light inspection. A low-light visible camera and a co-registered infrared module provide synchronized digital intensity frames; the application applies median filtering, histogram equalization, convolution, wavelet processing and Laplacian/wavelet fusion, then displays the enhanced or fused image locally. The proposed terminal uses two MIPI CSI-2 inputs, I2C/SCCB sensor configuration and SPI commands from a local user-control panel. It requires paired-frame buffering and display output rather than a network imagery service. Sensor calibration and geometric registration are upstream responsibilities.

benchmark_context.workload: Current main uses two synthetic 40x30 intensity images represented as float arrays, with default 10-bit input/output intensity ranges. It exercises single-image enhancement and two-image fusion ensembles.
benchmark_context.scenario_status: The visible/infrared pairing is a proposed use of the two-input fusion code, not evidence of real sensor capture or calibrated multispectral validation.
benchmark_context.validation_target: Compare enhancement and fusion image outputs with the CPU reference on identical input pairs; check ensemble checksums and define floating-point tolerances before acceptance. Real low-light image quality requires separate data.
benchmark_context.resource_note: Local display and dual acquisition are proposed integration requirements. Use the 13 mm^2 small-CPU budget for Ibex-oriented mapping, together with the 75 MHz and 28nm experiment settings, without claiming an achieved video frame rate.

communication.requirements: Require two MIPI CSI-2 camera receive channels, either as two instances or a documented dual-channel receiver, with frame markers suitable for pairing visible and infrared intensity images. A single unspecified receiver does not establish dual-input support.
Require I2C/SCCB sensor-register access to both independently addressed camera modules for exposure, gain and capture-mode configuration.
Require an SPI interface for user-panel commands selecting enhancement/fusion mode and output settings. The panel carries commands, not full-rate image pixels; Ethernet and USB are not required.

debug.requirements: Require hardware cycle and transaction counters to measure enhancement/fusion processing and display-buffer turnover.

analog.requirements: Both sensor modules deliver digital intensity samples; no on-chip analog image-sensor frontend is required.

audio.requirements: This viewing terminal has no audio acquisition or playback requirement.

video.requirements: Require independent strided frame buffers for the two input streams and an output ping-pong buffer. Preserve frame pairing while filtering and fusion use intermediate images.

Require a video-output/display controller that reads the enhanced or fused frame buffer and emits a pixel stream to a local display. A frame-buffer storage controller alone does not satisfy display output.

bus.requirements: Require SRAM scratchpad space for floating-point image intermediates, histogram/CDF/LUT arrays, convolution windows and transform workspace; derive capacity from the chosen resolution.
Require AXI shared-memory burst access between paired-frame storage, processing units and the display output controller.
Require AXI-Lite configuration, start, done and status registers for CPU sequencing of enhancement and fusion.
